News & Analysis on Domestic and International Trade, National and State Finances, Budget, Government Regulation, Monetary Policy, RBI Rates, Interest Rates, CRR, Indian Trade, Monetary and Industrial Policy.

item.title: Monsoon deficit raises risk of lower Rabi crop acreage
item.description: Farmers are likely to decrease rabi sowing due to inadequate rainfall and reduced soil moisture levels. This situation could lead to lower yields of critical crops such as wheat, pulses, and oilseeds. Many reservoirs are under pressure, with over half storing less than last year. State and central governments are encouraging farmers to choose crops based on water availability, especially in water-scarce regions.

item.title: Early crushing to shore up sugar supplies before Diwali
item.description: A quarter of Maharashtra's sugar mills will begin operations this week to alleviate sugar shortages before Diwali. Sugar prices have increased by approximately 4% recently due to dwindling supplies and farmer protests. Millers anticipate new sugar reaching markets after October 20, following crushing activities. Farmers are encouraging quicker harvesting of sugarcane due to crop conditions, leading to lower sugar content.

item.title: India working to develop China ties again, says Piyush Goyal
item.description: India's commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal highlighted ongoing efforts to improve relations with China while maintaining strong ties with the US. He emphasized that partnerships with trusted countries are essential for India's supply chain strategy. Goyal stated that India's economic and geopolitical concerns will shape its international engagement moving forward. The minister also addressed the need for self-sufficiency in critical sectors amid global disruptions.

item.title: India's data centre policy in works, says Jitin Prasada
item.description: India's government is preparing a data centre policy to enhance the hyperscale data centre sector. The proposed policy aims to streamline approvals and provide infrastructure status to the industry. A tax holiday until 2047 for eligible foreign cloud providers has also been announced. The use of artificial intelligence can improve power generation efficiency and flexibility for data centres.

item.title: Officials can deny benefits if tax relief found sole motive
item.description: India has implemented a Principal Purpose Test in the India-Mauritius Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement. This test allows tax authorities to deny benefits when tax relief is a principal purpose. The amendment, effective from August 2026, impacts various foreign investors using Mauritius for investments. The change affects significant cumulative foreign direct investment inflows into India from Mauritius. Experts believe this will alter how investment structures are evaluated under the treaty.

item.title: Insurers may face higher crop cover claims in Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Karnataka
item.description: In Maharashtra, insurers' liability could be capped at Rs 1,540 crore before the state government takes over claims beyond that level. The state has declared drought-like conditions in 265 talukas, raising concerns over this year's losses.

item.title: Wholesale inflation hits series high of 11.4% in September as fuel, food prices surge
item.description: India's wholesale inflation reached 11.4% in September, significantly increasing from 9.9% in August. Rising prices of fuel, food, and manufactured goods contributed to this surge. Food inflation climbed to 8.7%, marking a 23-month high. Retail inflation also saw an increase, rising to 5.54% year-on-year in September. Economists expect inflation to remain elevated in the coming months due to ongoing global commodity pressures.

item.title: CBDT nudges 12,000 tax professionals to file pending audit reports
item.description: CBDT has launched the SAKSHAM NUDGE campaign aimed at tax professionals to encourage timely filing of tax audit reports. The campaign targets those who filed fewer than 50% of their reports in the previous financial year. Messages were sent via SMS and email, urging quick compliance ahead of the new deadline. The deadline for submitting tax audit reports is extended to October 21, accommodating pending submissions. With over 19.

item.title: 'Data centres must be seen as strategic infrastructure': Niti Aayog report
item.description: Niti Aayog has released a report urging states to consider data centres as strategic infrastructure. The report suggests a structured approach to developing data centres sustainably. It highlights the need for common standards and guidance from the central government to support growth. Additionally, the report emphasizes the importance of assessing local resources and economic benefits. This framework aims to strengthen India's data-centre sector and its artificial intelligence economy.

item.title: NITI Aayog proposes higher social discount rate for project appraisal
item.description: NITI Aayog's working paper suggests increasing the social discount rate to 9.23% for project appraisal up to 30 years. This proposal aims to redefine economic viability for a variety of public investment projects in India. The revision has implications for ministries involved in long-term ventures such as infrastructure and energy. The paper also recommends specific rates for projects extending beyond 30 years.

item.title: Canada sees scope for more investments in India after Fairfax-IDBI bank deal, says Minister Sidhu
item.description: Canada's Minister of International Trade has noted the investment potential between Canada and India in infrastructure development. Following IDBI Bank's sale, Canadian companies aim to expand their presence in key sectors. The need for building additional airports in India presents opportunities for Canadian expertise in infrastructure and aviation. Canadian pension funds are also participating in several Indian infrastructure projects.

item.title: DGFT speeds up silver imports through IIBX, other nominated agencies
item.description: The government has simplified the procedure for obtaining import authorisations for specific silver items. This change should help genuine applicants receive approvals more quickly and efficiently. Import authorisations will only be available for purchases made through the India International Bullion Exchange or specified banks. Existing applicants will have the chance to revise pending applications using this new process.

item.title: Canada aims to seal India trade pact by year-end amid push to diversify ties
item.description: Canada aims to finalize a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement with India by the end of this year. Foreign Minister Anita Anand emphasized the need for diversifying trade partnerships beyond reliance on the United States. Indian trade negotiators recently visited Canada as both nations work to strengthen economic ties. A significant uranium supply agreement between Cameco and India illustrates growing cooperation between the two countries.

item.title: Centre set to cross Rs 80000 cr disinvestment target for first time since FY19 after IDBI Bank stake sale
item.description: The Indian government is expected to surpass its budgeted disinvestment target of Rs 80,000 crore for FY27. A significant contributor will be the strategic sale of IDBI Bank, which is valued at over Rs 52,878 crore. This sale includes the government's 30.48% stake alongside LIC's 30.24% stake in the bank. The total proceeds from various minority stake sales have already reached Rs 55,757 crore.

item.title: IDBI Bank strategic restructuring to attract FDI, boost banking sector, says FM Sitharaman
item.description: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved the strategic restructuring of IDBI Bank to attract foreign investments. The government retains a minority stake in the bank after its recovery, enabling further growth. Fairfax Financial Holdings will acquire a 60.72 percent stake in the bank for Rs 52,878 crore. The transaction aims to strengthen India's banking sector and reduce government ownership of state-run assets.

item.title: Cabinet clears Rs 53,428 crore for social assistance scheme, revises disability pension norms
item.description: The Union Cabinet has approved an outlay of Rs 53,428 crore for the National Social Assistance Programme. This approval will support the program's continuation from 2026-27 to 2030-31 with updated eligibility criteria. Monthly assistance rates for disability pension beneficiaries will increase with adjustments for age and disability severity.

item.title: Ultra-short-term borrowing costs spike; premium over policy rate hits 4-year high
item.description: The Reserve Bank of India hiked rates for the first time in nearly four years last week and shifted its stance, signalling more increases, while Governor Sanjay Malhotra on Tuesday said monetary policy cannot be seen as separate from financial stability, prompting traders to ramp up rate hike bets.

item.title: India's trade deficit with China crosses USD 100 bn in first 9-months
item.description: India's trade deficit with China has climbed to USD 105.93 billion in the initial nine months of this year. However, it is noteworthy that Indian exports to China saw a remarkable increase of 40.7 percent during this timeframe. Overall, bilateral trade has expanded by 25.4 percent, as China’s exports to India have also increased.

item.title: Cabinet approves 78-day bonus worth Rs 2,009 crore for 11.4 lakh railway employees ahead of Diwali
item.description: The Union Cabinet has approved a 78-day productivity-linked bonus worth Rs 2,009.61 crore for 11.4 lakh railway employees, with a maximum payout of Rs 17,951 per eligible employee. The decision follows record freight loading and passenger traffic in 2025-26, while railway staff associations continue to seek a higher bonus ceiling.

item.title: India's ultra-short-term borrowing costs spike; premium over policy rate hits 4-year high
item.description: India's 182-day and 364-day treasury bill yields climbed to 18-month highs at Wednesday's auction, while premiums over the RBI's 5.5% repo rate reached their highest levels since November 2022. Investors are factoring in further monetary tightening following the central bank's recent rate hike and hawkish guidance, market participants said.

item.title: We are working to develop relations with China once again: Piyush Goyal
item.description: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal stated that India seeks to improve relations with China, ensuring fair deals. Bilateral trade between India and China reached USD 127.7 billion, which reflects significant growth in exports and imports. Furthermore, Goyal expressed concerns regarding the widening trade deficit and tightened FDI policies due to geopolitical tensions. India experienced supply chain vulnerabilities during Covid, leading to a focus on self-sufficiency.

item.title: 85% of Maharashtra declared drought-hit; farmers to get Rs 5,000 aid before Diwali
item.description: Maharashtra's government has declared drought in over 305 talukas due to a severe rainfall deficit. Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis announced that Rs 5,000 will be deposited in farmers' accounts before Diwali. Efforts are being made to prevent coercive loan recoveries from farmers facing hardships. A zero-tolerance approach is being enforced against unauthorized water extraction to ensure drinking supplies.

item.title: India to roll out data centre policy as concerns grow over power use
item.description: India is preparing a dedicated data centre policy to address concerns over electricity consumption and protect consumers from higher power bills, Minister of State for IT Jitin Prasada said on Wednesday. The move comes amid local protests against planned Amazon and Google projects over water, electricity and environmental concerns.

item.title: WPI inflation quickens to 11.39% in September from 9.9% in August
item.description: Wholesale prices in India rose significantly to 11.39% in September, driven by rising fuel and food costs. Retail inflation also increased to 5.54%, attributed largely to higher vegetable prices. Concerns remain over food inflation maintaining elevated levels due to factors like uneven monsoon rainfall and El Nino risks. Increased global commodity prices are further affecting food production costs and transportation expenses.

item.title: India's inflation hits 5.54%: Onion prices up 108%, food inflation 7.74% | 10 numbers explained
India tightens Mauritius tax treaty rules to prevent misuse of tax benefits, effective August 10
item.description: The Finance Ministry has unveiled an important amendment to the India-Mauritius Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement. Effective August 10, the new Principal Purpose Test seeks to curb potential abuses of tax treaty benefits. This allows tax authorities to examine claims more thoroughly, specifically targeting investment vehicles based in Mauritius, such as foreign portfolio investors and private equity funds, to maintain fair taxation practices.

item.title: 'Don't worry': Piyush Goyal sends a message to the world on India-US ties
item.description: At the Bloomberg New Economy Forum, Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal shed light on the promising future of India and the US's partnership. He expressed his belief in the strong bond that is expected to grow, while addressing fears regarding its effects on other nations. Goyal confirmed that this alliance is stable and poses no threats, fostering a hopeful view for the future of their relations.

item.title: RBI open to more steps to curb FX speculation, Governor Sanjay Malhotra says
item.description: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra said the central bank may take further steps to curb speculative forex trading and ensure orderly movement in the currency market. He said recent restrictions aim to support genuine hedging needs, not impose capital controls.

item.title: Piyush Goyal meets Rishi Sunak, Czech minister; trade, tech partnerships on agenda
item.description: Union Minister Piyush Goyal met with Czech Republic Deputy Prime Minister Karel Havliček to discuss economic cooperation. He also had discussions with former UK Prime Minister Rishi Sunak regarding strengthening India-UK economic ties. The meetings emphasized collaboration in trade, investment, and technology partnerships between the nations involved. Goyal highlighted the importance of industry collaboration in enhancing economic relations and trade opportunities.

item.title: India-US trade deal heading towards ‘landing point’, EAM Jaishankar says
item.description: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar indicated that India and the US are advancing their trade deal negotiations. Both countries are addressing outstanding issues, with officials working diligently to find resolutions. Jaishankar emphasized that the negotiations are complex due to competitive agreements being made by the US with other economies. He noted the significance of tariffs in relation to the US's efforts to reindustrialize its economy.

item.title: FM Sitharaman ready to hear out stock market tax debate
item.description: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman expressed interest in the discussions surrounding stock investment taxes and their implications. She mentioned that changes to these taxes are highly anticipated ahead of the Union Budget. Additionally, Sitharaman noted that the Reserve Bank of India is working to manage rupee volatility through specific measures. She emphasized the importance of maintaining strong economic fundamentals during these discussions.

item.title: Ircon to monetise 4 highway assets; PSU plans to unlock 3,000cr value as part of GoI's infra monetisation
item.description: Ircon International has placed four highway assets for sale in a government-led monetisation programme. These assets include toll-road and hybrid annuity model projects located in Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Karnataka, and Gujarat. The enterprise value of the assets is estimated to be around ₹3,000 crore, as advised by Axis Capital. Currently, Ircon is a Navratna company primarily earning from its railway segment.

item.title: Bihar joins Maharashtra, UP in curbing sale of non-subsidised fertiliser
item.description: Bihar has imposed restrictions on the sale of non-subsidised fertilisers to control access for farmers. These restrictions could limit the availability of advanced crop nutrition products through existing distribution networks. Industry executives warn that this move may lead to significant losses and hinder investment in new technologies. Concerns have been raised about potential impacts on soil health and crop productivity.

item.title: MSMEs need to focus on quality, cost to gain from new FTAs: Secy
item.description: India's expanding network of free trade agreements is creating new opportunities for MSMEs to grow. The MSME ministry emphasizes the need for improved quality and cost competitiveness to access these opportunities. Moreover, government support for first-time exporters through practical assistance is crucial for success. It is essential to enhance certification participation and upgrade testing infrastructure to meet international standards.

item.title: GST must become an economic partnership, not just tax collection tool: CBIC chief Vivek Chaturvedi
item.description: Vivek Chaturvedi, Chairman of CBIC, emphasized the importance of reducing compliance burdens for GST taxpayers. During a recent meeting, various stakeholders discussed upcoming reforms focused on simplifying tax administration processes. Proposed changes include decriminalisation of certain offences and a higher threshold for prosecutions. The introduction of automated refunds and centralised administration aims to improve taxpayer experiences.

item.title: IMF raises India growth forecast to 7% as oil shock, AI reshape global outlook
Strong statistical systems key to achieving Viksit Bharat by 2047, says PM's principal secretary
item.description: India requires a reliable and technology-enabled statistical system to aid evidence-based policymaking. Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister P K Mishra emphasized the need for stronger state-level statistical institutions. He highlighted the importance of integrating data systems and using advanced technologies for accurate statistics. Mishra urged that more granular data is essential for assessing policy outcomes and addressing regional disparities.

item.title: PM GatiShakti: over 400 infra projects worth Rs 20.23 lakh cr recommended for approval
item.description: Over 400 infrastructure projects worth approximately Rs 20.23 lakh crore have been approved under the PM GatiShakti initiative. The initiative aims to reduce logistics costs by developing integrated infrastructure across India. It integrates more than 1,800 data layers covering various sectors, including transportation and telecommunication. The Network Planning Group reviewed these projects for investments exceeding Rs 500 crore. This digital platform enhances data-driven infrastructure planning and management throughout the country.

item.title: Scindia calls for faster tailored credit flow to Northeastern states at bankers' conclave
item.description: During a recent gathering at Mizoram University, Union minister Jyotiraditya Scindia urged financial institutions to provide credit solutions that address the specific needs of the Northeast region. He criticized generic banking products as insufficient, emphasizing customization for each state. Mizoram Chief Minister Lalduhoma shared initiatives requiring investment, hinting at potential economic drivers for the area that could facilitate sustained growth and enhance public welfare.

item.title: IMF's bullish call: Why is India sprinting when the world stumbles?
item.description: The IMF has raised India's growth forecast to 7% for both FY27 and FY28, highlighting the country's resilience despite higher oil prices and a slowing global economy. Strong domestic consumption, infrastructure spending, recovering private investment and AI-related capital expenditure are supporting growth, though inflation, energy costs and weaker rural demand remain risks.

item.title: Bayer’s DirectAcres crosses 2,00,000 acres in India
item.description: Bayer brings together its capabilities in Seeds & Traits, Crop Protection, Digital Farming Solutions and agronomy with tailored mechanization and digital advisory to support farmers through the transition.

item.title: Rupee volatility in focus as Sitharaman signals more RBI action, weighs LTCG tax debate
item.description: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said the RBI may take further measures to curb rupee volatility, clarifying that its aim is to stabilise the currency rather than fix its value. The rupee recorded its biggest single-day gain in six months on Monday after the central bank introduced curbs to reduce dollar demand and intervened in the market by selling dollars.

item.title: PM GatiShakti completes 5 years, next phase focuses on multimodal connectivity: Piyush Goyal
item.description: Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal on Tuesday said the PM GatiShakti National Master Plan would continue to support multimodal connectivity, faster infrastructure development and greater logistics efficiency as the initiative completed five years.

item.title: The Andaman Islands could be India's next big trade trump card
item.description: India is focusing on strengthening the Andaman and Nicobar Islands' strategic maritime role for regional trade. The upcoming Andaman Dialogue 2027 will emphasize maritime infrastructure and economic cooperation among countries in the Indo-Pacific region. Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal highlighted the islands as an economic bridge, particularly for trade and logistics efforts. Enhanced cooperation between regional ports and industries is also proposed to bolster maritime security.

item.title: SBI Research calls for abolition of LTCG tax on equities to boost foreign capital inflows
item.description: According to SBI Research, removing the long-term capital gains tax on equities could revitalize investment levels. The report emphasizes extending the holding period to two to three years as a strategy to boost investor morale. Faced with foreign portfolio outflows, the need for policy reforms is clear.

item.title: India, America expanding cooperation across sectors: US ambassador Sergio Gor
item.description: Kolkata and the United States are strengthening ties across sectors such as defence, IT, and healthcare. Recent military exercises involving 500 troops and significant investments showcase this growing partnership. American companies are establishing production facilities in India, contributing to economic development in both nations. India plays a crucial role in supplying generic medicines to the US, which enhancing trust.

item.title: Blackstone COO flags tech disruption, geopolitical conflicts as global risks; says India's investment climate improving
item.description: Blackstone President Jonathan Gray highlighted risks like technology disruption, geopolitical conflicts, and government debt affecting the global economy. He stressed India's progress in infrastructure and foreign investment, which enhance growth prospects. Gray indicated that simpler rules and clearer policies could help attract foreign capital and support nations facing fiscal constraints. Natarajan Chandrasekaran expressed concerns about technology misuse and labor market changes.

item.title: Canada to lead largest trade delegation to India in over 30 years, CEPA talks in focus
item.description: Canada is leading its largest trade delegation to India in more than 30 years, with nearly 300 business delegates set to explore partnerships across key sectors as both countries advance negotiations on a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), Canadian International Trade Minister Maninder Sidhu said.

item.title: PM Modi's free trade push could lead to $140 billion GDP gain for India
item.description: A more protectionist US could unexpectedly benefit India as New Delhi expands its free-trade agreements (FTAs) to diversify export markets and attract investment. A World Trade Organization-based model estimates that India’s concluded and proposed trade deals, including agreements with the EU and New Zealand, could add about $140 billion to GDP by 2035, lifting it 1.7% above the baseline.

item.title: IMF raises India’s FY27 growth forecast to 7%
item.description: The International Monetary Fund has increased India's economic growth projections for FY27 and FY28 to 7%. This adjustment reflects resilient domestic demand and strong performance in the services sector. India's GDP growth reached 7.8% in FY26, exceeding expectations during the April-June quarter. Additionally, other major institutions like the World Bank have raised India's growth forecasts as well.
